subject: Re: Next steps & eval plan for Bancorp model fit
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@bancorp.com>, Jane Smith <jane.smith@bancorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Post-call recap & proposed eval plan

Hi John / Jane,

Thanks again for taking the time today 	6 great conversation and helpful context on your claims processing use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

- Goal: Validate model fit for Bancorp customer-facing claim-summary assistant (accuracy on entity extraction + response correctness under privacy constraints).
- Success criteria (draft): >= 92% entity recall on our key fields; <= 3% hallucination rate on a 500-case sample; latency target < 250ms p95 on Redwood Dedicated.
- Proposed approach: run a Bancorp-specific eval on Redwood using your labeled dataset (schema attached) and our prompt suite + benchmark models (Redwood-13B-quant, Open-7B-compat, and a tuned Redwood-33B variant).

Next steps I suggest:
1) You share a 500-2,000 case sample in the attached CSV schema (pseudonymized - see data guidance in the runbook).
2) Our team runs a baseline sweep and returns a short report with per-model metrics, example failure modes, and recommended prompts/temperature settings (target: 3 business days after we receive the dataset).
3) If you want, we can schedule a short validation call to walk through the results and agree on a pilot config.

Attachments: bancorp-eval-dataset-schema.csv, redwood-eval-runbook.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Feel free to correct any of the success metrics above - I listed what we heard on the call.

Thanks!

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: John Doe <john.doe@bancorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Smith <jane.smith@bancorp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-call recap & proposed eval plan

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we share the sample:

1) Dataset format: your schema has columns for case_id, customer_age, claim_text, labels_entities (JSON array). Can you accept labels as a separate TSV with a 1:1 mapping to case_id? We have exports that come out that way.
2) Scoring: does your baseline scoring tool compute both strict and partial match for entity spans? We care about partial credit on split-token entities.
3) Privacy: we must keep the dataset in our cloud; can we run the eval in our VPC Private deployment, or do you require us to upload to Redwood-hosted? We have an internal review before anything leaves our account.

If you can confirm dataset acceptance and scoring details I'll route a pseudonymized sample to you (expected Monday).

	6John
Head of Product, Bancorp Claims
john.doe@bancorp.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@bancorp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-call recap & proposed eval plan

John - perfect, thanks. Once you drop the pseudonymized sample to the secure upload link in the runbook (or reply here if you prefer to share the S3 path), I'll kick off the baseline job and post the job id + link to the Redwood benchmark viewer.

Quick note on the baseline config we'll run: Redwood-13B-quant (fast), Open-7B-compat (cost baseline), Redwood-33B-tuned (quality baseline), prompt templates from the attached prompt-set (included in the runbook). Scoring will include token-F1, span-exact, hallucination detection (comparator against labels), and latency p50/p95.

If you want us to exclude any PHI-style columns even in pseudonymized form, let us know and we'll validate the ingestion mapping before the run.

Thanks - looking forward to the sample.

--
Dylan Brooks
Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@bancorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-call recap & proposed eval plan

John - great questions. Quick answers and plan below:

1) Dataset format: yes - we can ingest a separate TSV for labels as long as there is a unique case_id column that matches the primary CSV. I attached a small example to the runbook. Please ensure label JSON arrays are string-escaped in the CSV/TSV.

2) Scoring: our eval harness computes both strict and partial-match entity scoring. By default we report token-level F1 and span-level exact match; we'll include both strict and partial by model in the report. We'll also surface confusion on entity classes (e.g., claimant_name vs third_party).

3) Privacy & hosting: you have two options - (A) Share the pseudonymized file to us via the secure upload link and we run the eval on Redwood-hosted Dedicated nodes (we can put the data in an isolated project with limited retention and SOC2 controls), or (B) run the eval inside your VPC using Redwood Private; we'll deliver the eval harness as a Docker bundle + runbook so your infra team can run it locally. Option B typically adds ~3 days to setup (onboarding and access checks).

What we recommend for speed: send option A pseudonymized sample to the secure link and we'll run the initial baseline. If you prefer the VPC path for compliance, we can switch after baseline to run full evaluation there.

Attached: redwood-eval-runbook.pdf (contains sample TSV/CSV), bancorp-eval-dataset-schema.csv

Proposed timeline: we'll start baseline within 24 hours of receiving the sample and deliver a concise results deck within 3 business days.

Thanks - looping Dylan to the thread to coordinate the baseline run and HubSpot updates.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199
